claims.statement: Tom Allen was chosen to second Tommy Kelly of Baltimore against Billy Parkinson of Pottsville, Pa., at Acquia Creek, Vermont, in 1867.
Tom Allen pulled a navy pistol and announced he would kill referee William E. Harding if Kelly did not get the decision.
Tom Allen cut the ropes and carried Kelly out of the ring.
In 1867 Tom Allen was about 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighed about 164 pounds.
Tom Allen agreed to second Tom Kelly against Bill Parkinson at Acquia Creek in 1867.
Tom Allen agreed to financially assist Kelly's Baltimore backers and to make sure Kelly did not lose the fight.
Tom Allen pulled a huge revolver on referee Wm. E. Harding and threatened to shoot him if Kelly did not win.
Tom Allen cut the ropes so that Kelly's crowd could rush the ring, then carried Kelly out of the ring.
Referee Wm. E. Harding awarded the fight to Bill Parkinson on a foul by Allen and Kelly's men.
Tom Allen, of Cleveland, was one of the seconds for Elliott when Elliott fought Gallagher on Pieche Island, Detroit River, on November 12, 1868.
Elliott fought Gallagher for one hour and seventeen minutes over twenty-one rounds on Pieche Island.
Elliott claimed the fight after a rough-and-tumble finish, and the referee decided in his favor.
Tom Allen was one of Jimmy Elliott's seconds when Elliott beat Charley Gallagher for $600 on Peach Island, near Detroit (printed as November 12, 1968).
Tom Allen was training for the Davis fight in the neighborhood of Cleveland, Ohio.
Charles Convy Gallagher, a Cleveland fighter, was described as a warm friend of Tom Allen.
Bill Ryall signed the articles of agreement on behalf of Thomas Allen.
Tom Allen's friends at the making of the match were Harry Slade and Bill Ryall.
Tom Allen and Bill Davis went into training for their fight on December 7, 1868.
Bill Davis's fighting weight was 185 pounds, and Tom Allen would not carry so much.
Seven or eight men said to be backers of Tom Allen attacked Bill Davis at Doyle's, near the Fair Grounds, on Christmas night; one of them cut Davis's wrist with a knife.
On Christmas night 1868, at Doyle's near the Fair Grounds, rowdies said to be Allen's backers quarrelled with Bill Davis, and one cut Davis on the wrist with a carving knife.
Tom Allen trained on the Gravois road, about nine miles from St. Louis, under trainer Tom Kelly.
Bill Ryall and Tom Kelly were Tom Allen's seconds in the Davis fight.
Tom Allen made a collection on the boat for the benefit of Bill Davis, raising about $150 and adding considerably himself.
Bill Ryall and Tom Kelley were Tom Allen's seconds in the fight with Bill Davis.
After the fight Tom Allen collected a handsome contribution for Bill Davis.
As the boat neared the city, Tom Allen and Charles Gallagher nearly fought in the cabin, and the crowd kept them apart.
Patsy Reardon, who had recently come from Ireland, was to second Tom Allen against Charlie Gallagher.
Tom Allen chose Dan Ryan (printed as Daa Ryan) as his umpire.
Patsy Reardon and Jack Looney were Tom Allen's seconds in the fight with Charlie Gallagher.
Tom Allen was reported to have said he was England's champion and could whip any Irishman on this side of the Atlantic.
Patsy Reardon and John Looney seconded Tom Allen in his fight with Charley Gallagher.
Tom Allen was in good condition on 1869-05-07 and would not need much training; he was to go into training at once.
Tom Allen was training under his trainer, Sherman Thurston.

Tom Allen's weight at the time is printed as 'one basdred and sitty-Gre p urds' (probably one hundred and sixty-five pounds).

Tom Keho acted for McCoole and Wm. Carroll acted for Tom Allen at the final deposit.
Tom Allen was invited to the Laclede Jockey Club races with his trainers and would probably attend the last day.
The preliminaries of the Allen and McCoole match were arranged at Hennesy's saloon in the presence of Allen, Charley Gallagher and Looney.
Tom Kelley appeared for Mike McCoole when the preliminaries of the Allen match were arranged.
Jim Coyne was Tom Allen's mentor.
Tom Allen fought Charley Gallagher on Tuesday, August 17, 1869, under American colors: a silk handkerchief with an American eagle, stars and two American flags.
After the fight, Allen walked to Gallagher's corner to shake hands, and Gallagher struck at him spitefully without hitting him.
Riley told Allen to leave the ring because the crowd would murder him.
Tom Allen said he knew who fired the shot at Chouteau Island and that it was meant for him.
Tom Allen said there would be no more fighting until the stakes of the last fight were given up.

Tom Allen made a speech of thanks to his hearers at the reception.

Tom Allen had numerous friends in Cincinnati, judging by the tone of the Cincinnati press.
Tom Allen had a row with Sherman Thurston at the Buckeye House in Cincinnati; the Enquirer says it was settled with a drink and a handshake.
Tom Allen's backers rejected Mike McCoole's choice of stakeholder, Murray, fearing he would not pay out if Allen won.
Bill Carroll represented Allen's side in Cincinnati and had been there all week trying to settle the stakeholder dispute.
Mr. Thorweger of St. Louis, who had $1,100 interest in the stake advanced by Allen, went to Cincinnati to settle the stakeholder dispute.
Tom Allen said Mike McCoole was very good as a private citizen but stood No. 3 as a fighter, and had a bad crowd of backers.
Billy Carroll was authorized to make all arrangements for Tom Allen's fights.
